parts.title: UPSC Geography: Climate of India — The Monsoon
parts.intro: Today we study the 'Rhythm of India'. The Indian Monsoon is a complex meteorological phenomenon that dictates the life of millions. We explore the mechanism of the South-West and North-East monsoons, the role of the 'Jet Streams', and the impact of 'El-Nino' and 'La-Nina'. For UPSC, focus on the 'Onset and Retreat', the 'Rainfall distribution', and the 'Koppen classification' of Indian climate. This is the most conceptual part of Geography.

pages.title: Mechanism of Monsoon
pages.intro: The monsoon is driven by differential heating of land and sea, creating a low-pressure system that pulls moist ocean winds inland.

branches.label: Differential Heating
branches.value: Land heats faster than ocean, creating low pressure over N. India

branches.label: ITCZ Shift
branches.value: Low-pressure belt moves north to Ganga plains in summer

branches.label: Tibetan Plateau
branches.value: Acts as thermal engine, intensifying low pressure

branches.label: Jet Streams
branches.value: Upper-atmosphere winds shift to steer monsoon winds

pages.title: South-West Monsoon (June-Sep)
pages.intro: The South-West Monsoon delivers ~75% of India's annual rainfall from June to September via two branches, with intermittent dry spells.

blocks.text: Monsoon 'breaks' are dry spells lasting days or weeks, causing temporary drought despite the season's overall heavy rain.

pages.title: North-East Monsoon (Oct-Dec)
pages.intro: The retreating North-East Monsoon brings crucial rain to Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh coasts from October to December.

items.label: Significance
items.value: Rain for areas receiving little from SW monsoon

pages.title: El-Nino & La-Nina
pages.intro: El Niño and La Niña are Pacific Ocean climate patterns that respectively weaken and strengthen the Indian monsoon.

pages.title: Koppen's Classification
pages.intro: Koppen's system classifies Indian climates using letter codes based on temperature and rainfall patterns.

items.label: Amw
items.value: West Coast: Tropical, monsoon, dry winter

items.label: BShw
items.value: NW India: Semi-arid, hot, dry winter

items.label: Cwg
items.value: Ganga Plains: Warm temperate, dry winter, hot summer

blocks.text: First letter: A=Tropical (hot), B=Dry, C=Warm temperate (mild winter). Second: m=monsoon, S=steppe/semi-arid, w=winter dry season.

cards.front: What is the primary cause of the monsoon rain system?
cards.back: The monsoon rain system is caused by the differential heating of land and sea.

cards.front: Where does the ITCZ shift during the summer to help draw in monsoon winds?
cards.back: The ITCZ shifts northward to lie over the Ganga plains.

cards.front: Which geographical feature acts as a thermal engine to strengthen the low-pressure system over India?
cards.back: The Tibetan Plateau acts as a giant thermal engine.

cards.front: What percentage of India's total yearly rainfall is provided by the South-West Monsoon?
cards.back: The South-West Monsoon provides 75% of India's rain.

cards.front: What are the periods of little or no rain during the South-West Monsoon called?
cards.back: These periods are known as breaks in monsoon or dry spells.

cards.front: Which regions receive rainfall from the North-East Monsoon?
cards.back: The North-East Monsoon provides rain to the coast of Tamil Nadu and the coast of Andhra Pradesh.
cards.short: The Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh coasts

cards.front: What is the impact of El-Nino on the Indian monsoon?
cards.back: El-Nino usually leads to drought or a deficient monsoon in India.

cards.front: What is the impact of La-Nina on the Indian monsoon?
cards.back: La-Nina usually leads to good or excess rainfall in India.

cards.front: Which Koppen classification code represents the climate of India's West Coast?
cards.back: The code Amw represents the climate on India's West Coast.

cards.front: Which Koppen classification code represents the climate of the Ganga Plains?
cards.back: The code Cwg represents the climate of the Ganga Plains.
Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (where trade winds meet).

cards.front: Which monsoon gives rain to Tamil Nadu in winter?

cards.back: Periodic warming of surface waters in the Eastern Pacific, affecting monsoon.
